result.summary: The image shows a bridge overpass with a sidewalk and a painted bike lane. The environment is designed for high-speed vehicle throughput, lacking physical separation for vulnerable road users and visible crossing infrastructure.

hazards.name: Unprotected Bike Lane
hazards.description: The bike lane is only separated from vehicular traffic by paint, which provides no physical protection on a high-speed bridge.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide lanes and the bridge context encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians and cyclists.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Install physical barriers such as bollards or a concrete curb to separate the bike lane from the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting fixtures at a lower height specifically for the sidewalk to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection features marked continental crosswalks and curb ramps with tactile paving, but is heavily car-oriented with a gas station and large billboards. The environment lacks visible pedestrian signals and contains multiple conflict points due to wide driveway entrances for the adjacent commercial property.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where signals would typically be mounted.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: The wide, undefined entrance to the gas station creates multiple potential conflict points between pedestrians on the sidewalk and turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, adjacent to the gas station pumps.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing phases and improve safety.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and reduce the speed of vehicles turning into the side street.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Define and narrow the gas station entrances to reduce the area where pedestrians and vehicles conflict.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and signalized traffic control, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the wide roadway and lack of median refuges result in long crossing distances that increase pedestrian exposure to multi-lane traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a significant duration due to the width of the multi-lane roadway without a central refuge.

hazards.name: High-Speed Geometry
hazards.description: Wide travel lanes and large corner radii can encourage higher vehicle speeds during turns and through movements.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

result.summary: The intersection includes basic pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks, curb ramps with tactile warnings, and pedestrian signals. However, the presence of railroad tracks embedded in the roadway directly within the crossing area creates a significant trip and slip hazard.

hazards.name: Railroad tracks in crosswalk
hazards.description: Metal rails embedded in the pavement across the pedestrian path create a trip hazard and can be slippery when wet.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, crossing the roadway within the marked crosswalk area.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the travel lane with no horizontal separation or vertical barrier.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the roadway edge.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the existing transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: Install a curb extension to shorten the crossing distance and slow down right-turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Safe Rail Infill
interventions.description: Install specialized flange-way fillers to minimize the gap between the rail and pavement, reducing trip hazards for pedestrians and wheels.
